$comment: The PR gate's pinned baseline, not only a quarantine: the suites jest.gate.config.js does not run, plus the numbers .github/ci/jest-gate-check.mjs holds the gate to. REMOVALS ONLY for 'suites': the checker fails any PR that adds a path not present on the base branch, so an addition needs SA review and a visible override. Every entry was red on main at 'since'. The floors are raised by hand and never lowered without SA. Pinned 2026-10-04 from PR #210's first Linux run (813 suites / 15,813 tests), about 2% below it: a bulk-deletion backstop, not an exact count (G1 and G5 are exact). Workplan: docs/workplans/TEST_STRATEGY_AND_CI_TIERING_WORKPLAN.md section 0.
$refusalsComment: G8's ceiling on how many network connections the gate refuses (tests/jest-no-network.ts records them; a unit test must not reach the network). Note the SIGN: minSuites/minTests are floors that may only RISE, maxRefusedConnections is a ceiling that may only FALL, and the checker hard-FAILS a raise or a removal rather than noting it, because editing it up is exactly how a new leak would get waved through. PINNED 2026-11-06 AT 0, on main at c3204325 (the merge of PR #629, which stubbed the last leaking suite: the scheduler's audit write, which escaped its supabaseServer mock because AuditTrailService builds its own client with createClient). It is the maximum of three CI runs that all read 0 — 41985451525 (the PR), 41985980053 (the merge queue) and 41986483715 (main after the merge); main read 1 the night before, at 41931925128. THE MARGIN IS ZERO, deliberately, and that is not a pin without a buffer so much as a pin whose buffer would be a licence. The count is not perfectly deterministic, but it errs in ONE direction only: a floating promise's socket may never open if its worker exits first, so a real leak can go UNRECORDED. The converse cannot happen — no record exists unless a connection was actually attempted and refused — so every refusal counted is a real leaked call, and any ceiling above 0 would permanently wave one through. Measure it only where CI runs the gate: on Windows ~29 suites fail early on CRLF-sensitive source scans and never reach their leaking code. If this goes red, stub the seam the call goes through rather than touching this number: jest.mock('@/lib/supabaseServer', ...) for ordinary queries, or jest.requireActual('@/tests/helpers/silentAuditTrail') for the audit module, which bypasses that mock.
